results.title: Portable distribution and acceptance integration
results.summary: Implemented portable Pi Write For lifecycle/package/release/docs integration and verified the compiled writer artifact through Pi runtime, clean npm consumers, release planning, and aggregate checks. Contract verifier reported `VERIFY 2026-09-22-pi-write-for: commits=3/4 pass=16 fail=0 judgment=1`; human voice acceptance remains pending. — Cycle 2 addressed the prior blocking issues: publish planning now validates the selected services helper range, and check-package has a separate contract-only ESM consumer. Remaining findings are non-blocking gaps around generalizing tooling and keeping documentation examples/generated artifacts aligned with the spec; the implementation is commit-ready after considering those cleanups.
findings: medium/spec-deviation scripts/check-package.ts:290 — The check-package CLI still hard-codes services then writer instead of discovering and validating all public workspace packages as the spec requires → Iterate public workspace/release metadata and derive dependency tarballs instead of encoding only the two current packages

medium/spec-deviation docs/service-discovery.md:138 — The new Pi Write For service example remains prose-only; check-docs only compiles referenced fixture files, and no write-for consumer fixture was added despite the spec requiring the service example to compile as a fixture → Add a maintained write-for consumer fixture, reference it from the docs, and include it in docs validation

low/spec-deviation docs/ideation/2026-09-22-pi-write-for/context-map.md:38 — Generated ideation run/context-map changes are in the implementation diff but are not listed as Phase 4 deliverables, and the context map claims missing write-for consumer fixtures exist → Remove these generated artifacts from the phase commit or explicitly add/spec the intended maintained files
